Direct Taxes "The Slap on the Face" Paid directly by you to the government. It hurts more because you see the money leaving your bank account. Income Tax — On Salary, Business, Profession Capital Gains Tax — On Profit from selling Stocks, Property, Gold Corporate Tax — On Company Profits (22-25%) Securities Transaction Tax (STT) — On Stock Market Trades Dividend Distribution Tax — Abolished, now taxed in your hands Controlled by: CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes) under Ministry of Finance 🍔 2. Indirect Taxes "The Silent Pinch" Collected from you, but paid by the seller. You pay this every time you consume something. Hidden in the price. GST — Goods & Services Tax (Replaced VAT, Service Tax, Excise) Customs Duty — On Imported Goods (Why iPhones are expensive) Excise Duty — On Petroleum & Liquor (State revenue) Stamp Duty — On Property Registration (5-7%) Road Tax / Toll — On Vehicle Registration & Highway Usage Contr

Sweden supplements its automatic 
adjustment with a notional defined contribution 
system in which benefits are explicitly linked to 
contributions and longevity — arguably the most 
actuarially coherent pension design in the 
OECD. [PAGE 33]
29 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Germany: Caution and the Weight of History 
Germany, where the modern pension was 
invented, has been more cautious. The statutory 
retirement age has been raised from sixty-five to 
sixty-seven, to be phased in fully by 2031, but the 
government has resisted linking it to life 
expectancy automatically. The reasons are partly 
political — Germany's trade unions and social 
democratic tradition place high value on the 
concept of a fixed and predictable retirement age 
— and partly philosophical: there is a strong 
tradition in German social policy of treating the 
pension as a right earned by contribution, rather 
than a benefit calibrated continuously to 
actuarial conditions. France offers the most dramatic recent case study 
in the politics of pension reform — and in how 
quickly the arithmetic of demography can collide 
with the culture of a country. France has 
historically had one of the most generous

text: MODULE SELECTION Don't Learn the Market. Learn How to Look at It. Analysis is simply making sense of uncertainty. There are two ways to do this. Choose the lens that fits your mind. 🏢 Fundamental Analysis // THE BUSINESS VIEW Desi Logic: Like checking the engine, mileage, and service history before buying a second-hand car. You care about the quality . 🌱 For: Long-term thinkers & Investors 🧠 Focus: Profit, Management, Durability ⏳ Speed: Slow, deep, and calm ❓ Asks: "Is this company worth trusting?" Initialize Fundamental ➔ 📈 Technical Analysis // THE CROWD VIEW Desi Logic: Like checking Google Maps traffic before driving. You don't care why the jam exists, you just want to know when to move . ⚡ For: Active Traders & Timing 👀 Focus: Price Patterns, Volume, Trends 🏎️ Speed: Fast, visual, and reactive ❓ Asks: "Is now the right time to buy?" Initialize Technical ➔ ⚠️ System Note: No Wrong Choice You do not have to choose forever. Most successful investors use Fundamental to choose what to buy, and Technical to decide when to buy. Start with the one that feels less scary. You can switch anytime. 🌙

The number sixty-five was never really an 
answer to the question of when people should 
stop 
working. It

convenience invented in an era when most 
workers never reached it. As the world's 
population has grown older and healthier, the 
convenience has become less convenient — and 
the search for a better answer has become one of 
the more consequential policy debates of the 
early twenty-first century. What the international experience makes clear is 
that there is no single correct answer. Denmark's 
elegant 
automaticity,

democratic 
turbulence, Japan's incentivised flexibility, and 
Norway's 
gradual 
extension 
all 
represent 
genuine responses to the same underlying 
arithmetic — responses shaped by distinct 
labour markets, political cultures, and social 
contracts. The lesson is not that India should 
replicate any one of these models, but that the 
questions being asked in Copenhagen, Paris, and 
Tokyo will, in time, be asked in Delhi and 
Mumbai too. The demographic arithmetic is 
universal, even if the policy answers are not. References

text: 💰 Revenue (Sales) // Top Line The raw money a company receives from selling goods. It is the fuel. No revenue = No business. Desi Logic The "Galla" (Cashbox). A Kirana shop earning ₹1 Lakh vs ₹5 Lakh. More sales = More activity. ⚙️ Operating Income (EBIT) // Core Profit Earnings Before Interest & Tax. Shows if the actual business model is profitable before paying bankers or government. Desi Logic Restaurant earnings minus vegetables & chef salary. If this is zero, shut the shop. 💎 Net Profit (PAT) // Bottom Line The final money left after paying EVERYONE (Staff, Govt, Bank). This is what shareholders own. Desi Logic "Haath mein kitna aaya?" Huge sales mean nothing if rent and interest eat everything. 📊 EPS (Earning Per Share) // Your Share Total Profit divided by total number of shares. It tells you how much profit *your* one share earned. Desi Logic If family profit is ₹100 and there are 4 brothers, EPS is ₹25. If EPS grows, you grow. 🚀 ROE (Return on Equity) // The Gold Standard Measures how efficiently the company uses shareholders' money. >15% is excellent. <10% is poor. Desi Logic FD gives 7%. If a business takes your money and generates only 6%, why invest? Look for 15%+. 🏭 R

It's expensive, and if the Dal is bad, your dinner is ruined. 🍱 The ETF Thali An ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) is a pre-set Thali. Nifty 50 ETF: You get a spoon of Reliance, a bowl of HDFC, a slice of TCS. The Cost: Dirt cheap. (Expense Ratio: 0.05%). The Logic: You are betting on India's Economy , not one company's CEO. LEVEL 02: MECHANIC How does it actually trade? Mutual Funds trade once a day (NAV). ETFs trade Live like stocks. Stock Market (NSE) ⬇️ NIFTYBEES (The ETF) ⬇️ Holds 50 Real Stocks The Secret Keeper: Authorized Participants (APs) If everyone sells NiftyBees, price should crash, right? Wrong. APs (Big Banks) step in. If ETF price < True Value (NAV), they buy the ETF and sell the underlying stocks for a profit. This arbitrage keeps the price glued to the true value. The Idea That Is Replacing a Fixed Number 
 
What is emerging from the accumulated weight 
of these reforms is a gradual shift from the 
concept of a fixed retirement age to the concept 
of a flexible retirement window — a band of 
years within which individuals may choose, with 
appropriate incentives and penalties, to leave the 
workforce. The mechanics of this shift vary. In some 
systems, workers may draw a reduced pension if 
they retire before the statutory age, or a higher 
pension if they defer beyond it. In others, the 
accrual rate — the proportion of final salary or 
average earnings that each year of contributions 
delivers — is adjusted so that longer careers 
produce meaningfully better pensions. A smaller

text: 🛡️ System Logic 01 What is Insurance? (Risk Transfer) Insurance is not an investment. It is a contract where you pay a small "Service Fee" (Premium) to a massive entity, so that when a "Critical Error" (Death, Accident, Fire) occurs, they bear the financial cost instead of you. Brutal Truth: If you are buying insurance to "get money back," you are doing it wrong. That is a marketing trap. LEVEL 02: HARDWARE PROTECTION Health Insurance: The "Anti-Wipeout" Layer In the Indian context, medical inflation is roughly 14% . A single bypass surgery or a 10-day ICU stay can delete years of compounding in a week. 🚫 No Room Rent Cap If your policy has a cap (e.g., 1% of sum insured), and you take a better room, the company will cut your entire bill proportionally. It's a hidden kill-switch. 🚫 No Co-Pay Co-pay means you pay a percentage of every bill. This is fine for small things, but catastrophic for a ₹20 Lakh bill. Visualizing the decay of savings without Health Cover. LEVEL 03: LIFE PROTOCOL Term Insurance: Pure Death Benefit Most Indians buy "Endowment" plans (LIC style) because they "get money back." statutory retirement ages partially mitigate this

the pension age automatically to life expectancy,

phases. A member of a defined contribution

Based on the recommendations of the SMAC, comments received through 
public consultation and subsequent discussion with various stakeholders, the norms for 
determination of base price, price bands, call auction in pre-open session and close-out 
mark-up for ETFs are provided below: 
 
4. Base Price for ETFs 
 
4.1. Considering the operational challenges in usage of T-1 day closing NAV of the ETFs as 
base price, to start with, the base price for determination of price bands of ETFs shall be 
T-1 day Closing Price i.e. last 30 minutes of Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of 
the ETF. 4.2. In case there is no trading in the ETF during the last 30 minutes of T-1 day, then base 
price shall be the Last Traded Price (LTP) of the day. Further, in case there is no trade 
on T-1 day, then base price shall be the latest available closing NAV of the ETF. 4.3. The Base price shall be adjusted for corporate action(s), if any. 4.4. However, the Stock Exchanges and Asset Management Companies of Mutual Funds 
shall jointly address the operational challenges to implement the use of T-1 day closing 
NAV of the ETFs as the base price w.e.f. April 01, 2027. 5. Price Bands for ETFs 
 
5.1. For Equity ETFs and Debt ETFs (other than Overnight ETFs and Liquid ETFs):  
 
5.1.1. For Equity ETFs and Debt ETFs (other than Overnight ETFs and Liquid ETFs), there 
shall be dynamic price bands, with an initial price band of +10%, which can be flexed 
upto +20% after a cooling off period. 5.1.2. The cooling off period shall be of 15 minutes after trades are executed at or above 
9.90% and so on, during which trading shall continue within the prevailing price band.
title: Norms for Base Price, Price Bands, Call Auction in pre-open session and Close-out procedure for Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)

In 1950, life expectancy at 
birth in the OECD's founding economies was 
broadly in the low-to-mid sixties for men and the 
mid-to-high sixties for women. By 2024, OECD 
averages for life expectancy at birth were in the 
high seventies for men and the low-to-mid 
eighties for women. The gap between the 
retirement age — which largely stayed at sixty-
five across the post-war decades — and the age 
of death widened progressively with each 
generation. The actuarial consequence of this shift is 
straightforward to state and politically explosive 
to address. A pension system designed to pay 
out for an average of five to seven years of 
retirement now pays out for fifteen to twenty. The ratio of workers contributing to the system 
relative to retirees drawing from it has declined 
simultaneously, as lower fertility rates across the 
developed world have shrunk the cohort 
entering the workforce. The OECD projects that 
for every 100 people of working age, the number 
aged sixty-five or over will rise from 33 today to 
52 by 2050 across its member economies. The phrase used by pension economists to

movement

prices and yields move in opposite directions. A 
bond pays a fixed coupon. When market yields 
rise, a buyer pays less for it, so the price of the older 
bond falls. When yields fall, the price of paper 
already held rises. Modified duration measures the size of that 
movement. Pension Funds disclose durations near 
nine years for the Government Securities schemes. Convexity moderates the effect and makes the gain 
from a fall slightly larger than the loss from an 
equal rise. July 2026 was favourable to the NPS holdings in 
this aspect. The weighted average yield on the 
benchmark 10-year Central Government security 
eased 10 bps to 6.76%. This was the second 
consecutive month of softening after twelve 
months of increases. Yields firmed again in the 
second half as crude prices rose. The security 
closed 6 bps above its starting level, so the gain 
rests in the monthly average. Price is only half the account for a fund that still 
accumulates. Coupon income also moves with 
yields, but in the opposite direction to price. Over 
a holding period close to the portfolio’s own 
duration, the two effects offset each other. NPS

text: System is a wealth destroyer 📉 MAX DRAWDOWN — The Survival Metric The largest peak-to-trough decline before a new high is reached. Hedge funds treat this as their #1 risk metric because investors don't leave due to low returns — they leave due to pain. A fund that earns 30% per year but drops 60% in the middle will lose all investors during the drawdown, even if it eventually recovers. RISK METRIC CATEGORY: SURVIVAL USED BY: ALL HEDGE FUNDS // FORMULA Max DD = (Trough Value − Peak Value) ÷ Peak Value × 100 Example: Portfolio goes ₹10L → ₹6.2L → 12L. text: Equity Protocol Stop treating the market like a casino. Start treating it like a partnership deed. LEVEL 01: NOOB What is a Stock? (The Desi Analogy) Forget the BSE screen for a second. Let's talk about Raju's Momo Stall . Raju makes the best momos in Delhi. He sells 100 plates a day. He wants to open a big shop with AC, but he needs ₹10 Lakhs . He only has ₹5 Lakhs. 🤝 The Deal You give Raju ₹1 Lakh . In return, Raju gives you a piece of paper that says: "You own 10% of this business forever." That piece of paper is a STOCK . If Raju sells 1,000 plates next year, you get 10% of the profit (Dividend). If Raju sells the shop to Haldiram's for ₹1 Crore, your ₹1 Lakh becomes ₹10 Lakhs (Capital Appreciation). LEVEL 02: MECHANIC How the Engine Works Raju's paper certificate is physical. In the modern world, we use the Demat System . You (Buyer) ➡️ NSE/BSE (The Mall) ➡️ Seller (Exit) Critical Truth: The Secondary Market When you buy a share of Tata Motors on Zerodha/Upstox, Tata Motors does NOT get your money . You are buying it from another person (Uncle Sharma) who wants to sell it. The company only gets money once: during the IPO (Initial Public Offering). After that, it's just people

The policy repo rate stayed at 5.25% through July, 
and the MPC held it there again in August. This 
steadiness helps the NPS portfolio, because bond 
prices and yields move in opposite directions. A 
bond pays a fixed coupon. When market yields 
rise, a buyer pays less for it, so the price of the older 
bond falls.
